_**User (2026-06-30 13:15:58Z)**_

關於測網路情況 Antigravity CLI 給我以下回答

```
Q:  關於speedtest我們能不測速但只讓它列出現在IP資訊嗎？（適合測試VPN有沒有成功）
  （好像也有個網站可以直接 curl xxx.myip 啥的獲得？）

---

A:

好問題！兩種方式都可以：

## 1. 用 `curl` 查 IP（最快最簡單）

```bash
# 最常用的幾個：
curl ifconfig.me          # 只回傳 IP，乾淨
curl ipinfo.io            # 回傳 IP + 地理位置 + ISP（JSON）
curl ip.me                # 只回傳 IP
curl icanhazip.com        # 只回傳 IP
curl checkip.amazonaws.com # AWS 提供的
curl ipinfo.io/ip         # 只要 IP，不要其他 JSON
```

推薦 `curl ipinfo.io`，因為它會顯示 **IP、城市、國家、ISP**，一眼就能看出 VPN 有沒有生效：

```json
{
  "ip": "1.2.3.4",
  "city": "Tokyo",
  "region": "Tokyo",
  "country": "JP",
  "org": "AS12345 Some VPN Provider"
}
```

## 2. `speedtest` 本身

`speedtest` 沒有「只顯示 IP 不測速」的選項。不過你可以用 `-L` 列出附近伺服器，它的輸出會包含你的外部 IP 資訊，而且 **不會跑測速**：

```bash
speedtest -L
```

但這主要是列 server，IP 資訊不一定明顯。所以查 VPN 狀態的話，**`curl ipinfo.io` 是最佳選擇**——快、資訊完整、零依賴。

---

**TL;DR**: 
```bash
curl ipinfo.io    # VPN 檢查神器，一秒出結果
```
```

    86	# Environment variables honored:

299	
300	  if [[ "$_NET_PROXY_CACHE" == "none" ]]; then
301	    printf '%s\n' "proxy: unavailable (no \$LOCAL_PROXY_URL; no loopback port from ${__NET_PROXY_PROBE_PORTS[*]} reachable)"
302	    [[ -n "$shell_active" ]] && printf '%s\n' "  note: shell env still has proxy vars set -- run \`proxy-off\` to clear"
303	    return 1
304	  fi
305	
306	  local state="available"
307	  [[ -n "$shell_active" ]] && state="active   "
308	  local hint="(not exported; use \`withproxy\`, \`try_direct_then_proxy\`, or \`proxy-on\`)"
309	  [[ -n "$shell_active" ]] && hint="(exported in current shell)"
310	  local all_url all_source
311	  all_url="$(__net_all_proxy_url)"
312	  all_source="$source"
313	  [[ -n "$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL" ]] && all_source="LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL env"
314	
315	  printf '%s\n' "proxy: $state http=$_NET_PROXY_CACHE  source=$source  $hint"
316	  if [[ -n "$all_url" && "$all_url" != "$_NET_PROXY_CACHE" ]]; then
317	    printf '%s\n' "  socks=$all_url  source=$all_source"
318	  fi
319	}
320	
321	# Validate that the detected proxy can actually reach the public internet.
322	# ICMP ping does not honor proxy env vars, so use Google's HTTP 204 endpoint.
323	proxy-test() {
324	  local url="${1:-https://www.google.com/generate_204}"
325	  if ! command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
326	    printf '%s\n' "proxy-test: curl not found" >&2
327	    return 127
328	  fi
329	
330	  __net_detect_proxy
331	  if [[ "$_NET_PROXY_CACHE" == "none" ]]; then
332	    printf '%s\n' "proxy-test: no proxy detected (set \$LOCAL_PROXY_URL or start your proxy, then \`proxy-refresh\`)" >&2
333	    return 1
334	  fi
335	
336	  local all_url
337	  all_url="$(__net_all_proxy_url)"
338	  printf '%s\n' "proxy-test: http=$_NET_PROXY_CACHE  all=$all_url  url=$url"
339	  withproxy curl -sS -o /dev/null \
340	    -w 'proxy-test: http=%{http_code} remote=%{remote_ip} total=%{time_total}s\n' \
341	    --max-time 10 "$url"
342	}
343	
344	# Clear the cached detection and re-probe; call after toggling your proxy.
345	proxy-refresh() {
346	  __net_clear_proxy_cache
347	  __net_detect_proxy
348	  proxy-status
349	}
350	
351	# Optional auto-activation: when $LOCAL_PROXY_AUTO_ACTIVATE=1 is set before
352	# this file is sourced, silently call `proxy-on` if a proxy is detected.
353	# Set the env var in a machine-local shell file (or ~/.zshenv / ~/.profile) on
354	# machines that should always route through the loopback proxy.
355	if [[ "$LOCAL_PROXY_AUTO_ACTIVATE" == "1" ]]; then
356	  proxy-on -q
357	fi
358	
359	# --- Rootless Docker socket ---
360	# Point the Docker CLI at the user-scoped socket when rootless Docker is
361	# installed. Without this, `docker` defaults to /var/run/docker.sock (the
362	# rootful path) and fails with "Cannot connect to the Docker daemon".
363	# Guarded on socket existence so this is a no-op on:
364	#   - macOS (OrbStack / Docker Desktop publish their own sockets, don't need this)
365	#   - Linux boxes still running rootful Docker (the rootful socket is under /var/run)
366	# Respect a pre-existing $DOCKER_HOST so a user-set value wins.
367	# See docs/tools/container-config-map.md for the full install-variant map.
368	if [[ "$(uname -s)" == "Linux" && -z "$DOCKER_HOST" ]]; then
369	  _net_xdg_runtime="${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/run/user/$UID}"
370	  if [[ -S "${_net_xdg_runtime}/docker.sock" ]]; then
371	    export DOCKER_HOST="unix://${_net_xdg_runtime}/docker.sock"
372	  fi
373	  unset _net_xdg_runtime
374	fi
375
```

1	# Custom Aliases & Shell Functions
2	
3	Quick reference for custom aliases and shell functions defined in this dotfiles repo. Available in zsh, bash, or both — the source file path tells you which:
4	
5	- `dot_config/shell/*.sh` — POSIX layer, sourced by **both** `~/.zshrc` and `~/.bashrc`.
6	- `dot_config/zsh/*.zsh` (or `tools/*.zsh`) — **zsh-only**.
7	- `dot_config/bash/*.bash` — **bash-only**.
8	
9	> **Maintenance rule** (mirrored in `CLAUDE.md`): whenever you add, modify, or remove a custom alias or shell function in `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/`, update this table — include the type (`alias` or `function`), source file (relative to repo root), and a one-line description. Place new helpers in the right tier per the [CLAUDE.md three-tier rule](../../CLAUDE.md#custom-aliases--shell-functions--docsshellsaliasesmd).

557	### Proxy helpers
558	
559	> Portable loopback-proxy helpers. Honors `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` (+ optional `$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL` for split Clash `socks-port:` configs); otherwise prefers an active Clash config (`mixed-port:` or `port:`/`socks-port:` from `~/.config/clash/config.yaml` or `~/Library/Application Support/clash/config.yaml`) before falling back to probing ports 7890/7891/1087/8118/8080 with `nc -z -w1`. Detection is cached per shell; `proxy-off` and `proxy-refresh` clear that cache before the next lookup. Set `$LOCAL_PROXY_AUTO_ACTIVATE=1` to auto-export env vars on shell startup. Full guide: [docs/tools/web-reader.md](../tools/web-reader.md). See also: [docs/tools/containers.md](../tools/containers.md) for how `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` feeds the chezmoi-managed `~/.docker/config.json` `proxies.default` block.
560	
561	| Command | Type | Source File | Description |
562	|---------|------|-------------|-------------|
563	| `withproxy` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Run a single command with proxy env vars exported to the child only (e.g. `withproxy curl ...`) |
564	| `try_direct_then_proxy` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Run a command direct; on failure, retry via `withproxy`. Used as the default for reader functions. |
565	| `proxy-on` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Export `http_proxy`/`https_proxy`/`HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`/`ALL_PROXY` in the current shell |
566	| `proxy-off` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Unset all proxy env vars in the current shell |
567	| `proxy-status` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Report state: **active** (exported), **available** (detected), or **unavailable** |
568	| `proxy-test` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Test detected proxy egress with `curl https://www.google.com/generate_204` (HTTP, not ICMP ping) |
569	| `proxy-refresh` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Clear cached detection, re-probe, print status (use after toggling your proxy) |

655	
656	## macOS apps
657	
658	> Graceful GUI app control via `osascript` + Apple Events. Prefer over `killall` for apps with state (OrbStack, Docker Desktop, Slack, etc.) — `quit` sends ⌘Q-equivalent, letting the app tear down cleanly. App NAME is the AppleScript name (e.g. `OrbStack`, `Google Chrome`), not bundle ID; passed via `osascript argv` so spaces/quotes are safe.
659	
660	| Command | Type | Source File | Description |
661	|---------|------|-------------|-------------|
662	| `appquit <AppName>` | function | `dot_config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh.tmpl` (macOS), `dot_config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl` (Linux) | **Cross-platform.** macOS: Quit Apple Event (graceful, equivalent to ⌘Q). Linux: `pkill -TERM -f <pattern>` resolved from `~/.config/shell/linux-apps.conf` overrides or auto-derived from `.desktop` scan; Electron + Firefox honour SIGTERM as graceful quit. |
663	| `applaunch <AppName>` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform.** macOS: launch in background (no focus steal). Linux: `gtk-launch <desktop-id>` via `setsid -f`. App-defined startup behaviour applies. |
664	| `appactivate <AppName>` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform.** macOS: launch + bring to front. Linux: D-Bus call to GNOME `window-calls` extension if installed (best fidelity), otherwise falls back to `applaunch` (single-instance apps re-focus). |
665	| `apprestart <AppName>` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform.** `appquit` + poll until process gone (≤15s) + `applaunch`. On Linux, launches the app even if it wasn't running (mirrors macOS silent-quit semantics). |
666	| `apprunning <AppName>` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform.** Silent predicate; exit 0 if running, 1 otherwise. Linux backend: `pgrep -f <pattern>`. |
667	| `applist [--pids\|--all]` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform.** Default: names of running apps the helper recognises. `--pids` adds `<pid>\t<name>` (used by `tv {mac,linux}-apps`). macOS lists foreground GUI apps via System Events; Linux enumerates registered overrides + auto-derived from `.desktop` scan filtered to running processes. Linux `--all` shows non-running entries too. |
668	| `appresponsive <AppName> [TIMEOUT_SEC]` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform, divergent fidelity.** macOS: best-effort "Not Responding" via timed-out Apple Event. Linux: only meaningful for apps registered with `--mpris=NAME` (Spotify, mpv, VLC); for Electron/Firefox/most apps it degrades to `apprunning` with a stderr note — no public Linux API analog to macOS Apple Events. |
669	| `linux_app_register NAME [OPTS]` | function | `dot_config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl` | **Linux-only.** Register an app for the Linux `app-*` helpers — `--desktop=ID --pkill=REGEX --wm-class=CLASS [--mpris=NAME]`. Typical call site: `~/.config/shell/linux-apps.conf` (sourced at shell startup, never auto-stubbed). Override file matters for AppImage / Snap / Flatpak where auto-derivation can't resolve the runtime binary path — see `pitfalls/linux-app-control-appimage-runtime-path.md`. `linux_app_register --list` prints the current registry. |

712	## Tmux Integration
713	
714	> Requires tmux + OSC 133 markers in the pane's scrollback (emitted by [`02_shell_integration.zsh`](../../dot_config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh) — if missing, run `exec zsh` to reload). All three functions print to stdout (pipe-friendly: `cpout | grep ERROR`) AND copy to the system clipboard via tmux's OSC 52 bridge. Shell-level counterparts of the `prefix + M-y` / `M-i` tmux bindings — see [docs/tools/tmux/README.md → OSC 133](../tools/tmux/README.md#osc-133-command-boundary-navigation-warp-style).
715	
716	| Command | Type | Source File | Description |
717	|---------|------|-------------|-------------|
718	| `cpout [N]` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/03_tmux_capture.zsh` | Print + copy the **Nth-latest command's output** (default N=1). Accepts positional integer for lookback |
719	| `cpcmd [N]` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/03_tmux_capture.zsh` | Print + copy the **Nth-latest command's input line** (default N=1). Reads zsh history so works outside tmux too |
720	| `cpblock [N]` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/03_tmux_capture.zsh` | Print + copy the **Nth-latest command's full block** (prompt + input + output). Default N=1 |
721	| `tsum [-d\|--shallow] [-r] [-i] [--sort closability] [--only TIER] [--dry-run]` | function | `dot_config/shell/61_tmux_summary.sh` | AI-summarize every tmux session — one-glance "what is this session", with closability tiers (🟢 safe / 🟡 check / 🔴 keep). Reuses the AI Capture agent fallback (claude / opencode / codex / cursor-agent); 10-min cached in `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/tmux-session-summary/`. `-d` includes the visible area of each session's active pane (20-100 lines, self-capture skipped); set `TSUM_DEEP_DEFAULT=1` in `~/.shellrc.adhoc` to make `-d` implicit (override with `--shallow`). `--sort closability` orders keep → check → safe (default: alphabetical); `--only {safe,check,keep}` filters to one tier. `-r` bypasses cache; `-i` opens fzf picker that switches client on Enter (also reachable via tmux `prefix + Space → Sessions → AI session summary`); `--dry-run` prints the prompt without calling the LLM. **On hosts with multiple tmux binaries** (apt + appimage, brew + system) export `TSUM_TMUX_BIN=/path/to/tmux` so tsum talks to the right server. |

725	## AI Capture
726	
727	> One-shot pipeline: capture a past block (via `cpblock N`) and pass it to a coding-agent CLI (opencode / claude / codex / agyc / cursor-agent) in non-interactive / advisory mode. Agent auto-detected in `$AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY` order; override with `-a AGENT`. Prompt override via `-p PROMPT`. Agent reply goes to stdout (pipe-friendly: `aifix | tee /tmp/advice.md`), status line to stderr.

730	|---------|------|-------------|-------------|
731	| `aifix [N] [-a AGENT] [-p PROMPT]` | function | `dot_config/shell/04_ai_capture.sh` | Capture Nth block (tmux), ask agent to diagnose + suggest a fix |
732	| `aiexplain [N] [-a AGENT] [-p PROMPT]` | function | `dot_config/shell/04_ai_capture.sh` | Capture Nth block (tmux), ask agent to explain what happened |
733	| `aifix-stdin [-a AGENT] [-p PROMPT]` | function | `dot_config/shell/04_ai_capture.sh` | Non-tmux: read stdin as context, ask agent (`tail -100 log \| aifix-stdin`) |
734	| `aifix-run -- CMD [ARG...]` | function | `dot_config/shell/04_ai_capture.sh` | Non-tmux: run CMD with stdout+stderr teed, feed to agent |
735	| `aifix-rerun [-y]` | function | `dot_config/shell/04_ai_capture.sh` | Non-tmux: thefuck-style re-execute last command (confirms unless `-y`; side-effect warning) |
736	| `aiblock` | function | `dot_config/shell/04_ai_capture.sh` | Launch the `scripts/aiblock.py` TUI: pick command(s) from history, edit prompt, pick action (print / copy / spawn new agent window). Deps resolved via `uv run --script` |

740	## AI Run
741	
742	> Quick "run one prompt through a coding agent" wrappers — fresh prompt, streams the reply straight back. Mnemonic mirrors the agent-session tags in `dot_config/television/cable/agent-sessions.toml` (`[oc]`/`[cc]`/`[cx]`/`[cu]`/`[ag]`), so muscle memory carries between `tv agent-sessions` (browse old) and these (start new). Extra flags pass through to the underlying CLI: `ccr -c 'continue'` → `claude -p --model haiku -c 'continue'` resumes the last session. Differs from [AI Capture](#ai-capture) which is capture-and-diagnose, not arbitrary-prompt.

745	|---------|------|-------------|-------------|
746	| `ocr [opencode flags] <prompt>` | function | `dot_config/shell/05_ai_run.sh` | `opencode run -m $AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL "<prompt>"` — agent tag `[oc]` |
747	| `ccr [claude flags] <prompt>` | function | `dot_config/shell/05_ai_run.sh` | `claude -p --model $AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL "<prompt>"` — agent tag `[cc]` |
748	| `cxr [codex flags] <prompt>` | function | `dot_config/shell/05_ai_run.sh` | `codex exec -m $AICAP_CODEX_MODEL "<prompt>"` — agent tag `[cx]` |
749	| `cur [cursor-agent flags] <prompt>` | function | `dot_config/shell/05_ai_run.sh` | `cursor-agent -p --model $AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL "<prompt>"` — agent tag `[cu]` |
750	| `agr [agy flags] <prompt>` | function | `dot_config/shell/05_ai_run.sh` | `agyc -p "<prompt>"` — Antigravity CLI; agent tag `[ag]`. `agyc` is a collision-free symlink → `~/.local/bin/agy` (the IDE squats bare `agy`); no `--model` flag (model is account-side) |
751	| `antigravity-cli` / `agy-ide` | alias | `dot_config/shell/05_ai_run.sh` | `antigravity-cli` → the Antigravity CLI (`agyc`); `agy-ide` → the Antigravity IDE editor launcher (defined only where the IDE is installed) |

```sh
# 50_networking.sh - Networking tool aliases and helpers (shared bash + zsh).
# Moved from dot_config/zsh/tools/50_networking.zsh; the only zsh-isms were
# `print -r --` / `print -u2` / `print "..."` which all became `printf`.

# --- Listening ports (works everywhere, no extra install needed) ---
alias ports='lsof -i -P -n | grep LISTEN'

# --- IP address helpers ---
alias myip='curl -s https://ifconfig.me'
if [[ "$OSTYPE" == darwin* ]]; then
  alias localip='ipconfig getifaddr en0'
else
  # shellcheck disable=SC2142  # `\$1` is awk's field-1, not a shell positional.
  alias localip='hostname -I | awk "{print \$1}"'
fi

# --- nmap shortcuts ---
if command -v nmap &>/dev/null; then
  # Quick ping sweep of local /24 subnet
  pingsweep() {
    local ip
    if [[ "$OSTYPE" == darwin* ]]; then
      ip=$(ipconfig getifaddr en0 2>/dev/null)
    else
      ip=$(hostname -I 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')
    fi
    local base="${ip%.*}.0/24"
    echo "Scanning $base ..."
    nmap -sn "$base"
  }
fi
```

Key structural conventions observed throughout the file:

- One-line header comment: `# NN_filename.sh - brief description (shared bash + zsh).`
- Section banners: `# --- Section name ---` with tool name and one-line purpose
- Tool guards: every non-trivial block is wrapped in `if command -v <tool> &>/dev/null; then ... fi`
- OS guards: `[[ "$OSTYPE" == darwin* ]]` vs `else` for Linux
- Private helpers prefixed `__net_` (double-underscore + module prefix); public functions use kebab-case (`proxy-on`, `proxy-off`, `proxy-status`, `proxy-refresh`, `proxy-test`, `withproxy`, `try_direct_then_proxy`)
- All user-facing output goes through `printf '%s\n'` (not `echo`, not zsh `print`)
- Variables cached per-shell are declared with `: "${VAR:=}"` before use

557	### Proxy helpers
558	
559	> Portable loopback-proxy helpers. Honors `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` (+ optional `$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL` for split Clash `socks-port:` configs); otherwise prefers an active Clash config (`mixed-port:` or `port:`/`socks-port:` from `~/.config/clash/config.yaml` or `~/Library/Application Support/clash/config.yaml`) before falling back to probing ports 7890/7891/1087/8118/8080 with `nc -z -w1`. Detection is cached per shell; `proxy-off` and `proxy-refresh` clear that cache before the next lookup. Set `$LOCAL_PROXY_AUTO_ACTIVATE=1` to auto-export env vars on shell startup. Full guide: [docs/tools/web-reader.md](../tools/web-reader.md). See also: [docs/tools/containers.md](../tools/containers.md) for how `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` feeds the chezmoi-managed `~/.docker/config.json` `proxies.default` block.

# Plan: IP Geo / VPN-check shell functions

## Context

The existing `myip` alias (`curl -s https://ifconfig.me`) returns only a raw IP —
good for scripting but useless for verifying whether a VPN is actually routing
traffic through the intended exit node. `ipinfo.io` returns structured JSON
(ip / city / region / country / org) in a single call, making it the right tool for
a one-glance VPN check. This plan adds `ipgeo` + `vpncheck` to the existing
networking helper file and documents them.

## Service comparison (reference, not written to any file)

| `curl` target | Output | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| `ifconfig.me` | raw IP | scripting (`myip` alias) |
| `ipinfo.io` | JSON: ip, city, region, country, org | VPN verification ← **use this** |
| `ipinfo.io/ip` | raw IP | same as ifconfig.me |
| `ip.me` | raw IP | bare alternative |
| `icanhazip.com` | raw IP | Cloudflare-backed alternative |
| `checkip.amazonaws.com` | raw IP | AWS-backed alternative |

`ipinfo.io` wins for VPN checking because it bundles geo + ISP in one call
with no extra flags. The others all require a second call or an API endpoint
suffix to get geo info. Keep `myip → ifconfig.me` as-is (plain IP,
scriptable, zero-JSON-parsing).

## Changes

### 1. `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh`

Append under the `# --- IP address helpers ---` section (after line 15),
**before** the `# --- nmap shortcuts ---` block:

\```sh
# ipinfo.io returns JSON (ip/city/region/country/org) in one call; better than
# ifconfig.me for VPN exit-node checks where you need the ISP/country at a glance.
ipgeo() {
  if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
    curl -s https://ipinfo.io | jq -r '"IP:      \(.ip)\nCity:    \(.city)\nRegion:  \(.region)\nCountry: \(.country)\nOrg:     \(.org)"'
  else
    curl -s https://ipinfo.io
  fi
}
alias vpncheck='ipgeo'
\```

No tool guard needed — only `curl` (already a baseline assumption in this
file) and optionally `jq` (graceful fallback to raw JSON).

### 2. `docs/shells/aliases.md`

In the **Networking** table (around line 543), add two rows after the
existing `myip` row:

\```
| `ipgeo` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Public IP + city / country / ISP via ipinfo.io; jq-pretty if available, raw JSON fallback |
| `vpncheck` | alias | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Alias for `ipgeo` — one-glance check that VPN exit node is the expected country/ISP |
\```

No other files need updating (this is a pure-curl function with no new
install dependency, so `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md` is unaffected).

## Verification

\```sh
# After chezmoi apply (or `source ~/.config/shell/50_networking.sh`):
ipgeo          # should print IP / City / Region / Country / Org
vpncheck       # same output (alias)

# With VPN on vs off — Country and Org should differ
# Without jq:  PATH_OVERRIDE=$(which jq) unset jq; ipgeo  # raw JSON
\```

All good. Here's the summary:

**`-L` / `--servers`**: no client IP at all — just a server list with locations.

**Full run with `--format=jsonl --progress=no | head -1`**: emits a `testStart` object immediately with `isp`, `externalIp`, and notably **`isVpn: true/false`** (Ookla's own VPN detection). The `head -1` causes SIGPIPE which kills speedtest before download begins — takes ~5s vs a full 20-30s run.

Three functions added to `50_networking.sh` + docs updated:

| Command | Speed | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| `myip` | ~1s | raw IP only (unchanged, scriptable) |
| `ipgeo` / `vpncheck` | ~1s | IP + city + country + ISP (ipinfo.io) |
| `speedtest-info` | ~5s | ISP + IP + `isVpn` boolean (Ookla's own detection) |

The `speedtest-info` approach is overkill for everyday use but has one unique edge: the `isVpn` boolean comes from Ookla's server-side detection, so it can catch VPN exits that ipinfo.io doesn't flag.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-06-30 13:33:37Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-06-30 13:33:51Z)**_

主要是**兩層偵測**疊加：

## 1. Client-side：網路介面名稱 + MAC 位址

從我們實測的輸出可以直接看到線索：

```json
"interface": {
  "internalIp": "198.18.0.1",
  "name": "utun5",           ← macOS TUN 介面
  "macAddr": "00:00:00:00:00:00",  ← 虛擬介面沒有真實 MAC
  "isVpn": true
}
```

speedtest CLI 查看**目前路由預設閘道走哪張網卡**：
- `utun*` / `tun*` / `tap*` / `wg*` / `nordlynx` 等前綴 → 幾乎確定是 tunnel 介面
- MAC 全零 → 虛擬介面（真實網卡不會這樣）

這個判斷完全在本機完成，不需要連網路。

## 2. Server-side：IP 信譽資料庫（ASN lookup）

我們的 `externalIp` 是 `48.210.71.128`，ISP 是 `"Microsoft Azure"`。Ookla 的伺服器對所有連進來的 IP 做 **ASN 查詢**：

- Azure / AWS / GCP / DigitalOcean / Linode 的 IP 段都被標記為 datacenter/hosting ASN
- 商業 VPN 業者的 IP 段也早已被標記（MaxMind、IPinfo、Ookla 自建的 IP 情資庫）

## 為什麼兩層都要？

| 情境 | 介面偵測 | IP 信譽 |
|---|---|---|
| 家用 VPN（自架在 Azure）| ✓ utun 介面 | ✓ Azure ASN |
| 企業 VPN（exit 是公司靜態 IP）| ✓ utun 介面 | ✗ 公司 IP 不在黑名單 |
| 翻牆但走 tun2socks 系統 proxy 模式 | ✗ 走預設 en0 | ✓ IP 在 VPN 業者 ASN |
| Tor exit node | ✗ 走一般 TCP | ✓ Tor exit IP 全部在名單 |

所以兩個條件 OR 起來才能覆蓋大多數情況。`isVpn: true` 的 false negative 主要發生在「VPN 走 HTTP/SOCKS proxy 模式但不建 tun 介面，且 exit IP 也不在資料庫」的邊角案例。

```md
---
name: ref-speedtest-vpn-detection
description: How Ookla speedtest CLI detects isVpn in testStart JSON — client-side interface name + server-side ASN lookup
metadata:
  type: reference
---

`speedtest --format=jsonl --progress=no | head -1` emits a `testStart` object before any download/upload. It includes:

\```json
"isp": "Microsoft Azure",
"interface": {
  "internalIp": "198.18.0.1",
  "name": "utun5",
  "macAddr": "00:00:00:00:00:00",
  "isVpn": true,
  "externalIp": "48.210.71.128"
}
\```

**Two-layer VPN detection (OR'd together):**

1. **Client-side — interface name + MAC**: speedtest CLI checks which interface holds the default route. `utun*`/`tun*`/`tap*`/`wg*`/`nordlynx` prefixes → tunnel. `macAddr: "00:00:00:00:00:00"` → virtual (no real NIC). Fast, no network call needed.

2. **Server-side — ASN/IP reputation**: Ookla's servers look up the client's `externalIp` against datacenter/VPN ASN databases (similar to MaxMind GeoIP2 Connection Type). Commercial VPN provider IPs and cloud ranges (Azure/AWS/GCP) are pre-tagged.

**Coverage gaps (false negatives):** VPN running in HTTP/SOCKS proxy mode (no tun interface created) with an exit IP not in the reputation database.

**Shell function added:** `speedtest-info` in `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` — grabs the `testStart` line via SIGPIPE (`head -1`), ~5s total. For everyday VPN checks, prefer `vpncheck` (`curl ipinfo.io`, ~1s).

```

1	# Dotfiles Repo Memory
2	
3	## Ansible on macOS
4	- `ansible.builtin.unarchive` with `.tar.gz` fails on macOS because it requires GNU tar, but macOS ships BSD tar. Use `.zip` assets instead (macOS has `/usr/bin/unzip` built-in).
5	- The ansible runner script (`run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl`) only passes `BECOME_FLAGS` (sudo) on Linux, not macOS. Any `become: true` task will fail on macOS with "sudo: a password is required". Put macOS sudo operations in shell scripts instead.
6	
7	## SpecStory
8	- Correct GitHub repo for releases: `specstoryai/getspecstory` (not `specstoryai/specstory`)
9	- Asset naming: `SpecStoryCLI_{Darwin,Linux}_{arm64,x86_64}.{tar.gz,zip}`
10	- Tarball contains single `specstory` binary at root level
11	
12	## Chezmoi script naming
13	- `run_once_before_*` — runs once ever (bootstrap)
14	- `run_before_*` — runs every `chezmoi apply`
15	- `run_onchange_after_*` — runs when hash in script changes
16	
17	## Homebrew / toolchain gotchas
18	- [Homebrew aliyun auto-update hang](homebrew-aliyun-autoupdate-hang.md) — `brew install` stalls (lock held for days) on the aliyun mirror's update fetch; use `HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`. Also: stale Go 1.15.4 at `/usr/local/go/bin` breaks source builds.
